purpose: MorphoWeave is a 3D Slicer extension for digital-morphology workflows: it builds mean anatomical atlases and dense correspondences from meshes plus sparse landmarks (Atlas Builder), fits and explores PCA statistical shape models (Model Library), transfers template landmarks to new specimens with rigid + SSM-guided deformable registration (Landmark Transfer), and segments homologous surface regions (Surface Segmentation). Its users are morphometricians and anatomy researchers working on surface models, not clinicians.
summary: No network transmission, no torch, no unsafe deserialization (np.load with allow_pickle=False), and runtime pip installs go through slicer.packaging.pip_ensure with explicit user confirmation. BSD 2-Clause license plus third-party notices for the DeCAL-derived code; catalog entry is consistent with CMake (EXTENSION_DEPENDS empty, build_dependencies empty). Remaining issues are non-blocking: Model Library ingest does not validate the database name (path traversal / writing outside the library root, unlike Atlas Builder's isSafeLibraryName), pip_uninstall of tiny3d/tiny3d-rs touches the shared Slicer environment, README/EXTENSION_ICONURL reference logo.png and Docs/Media/morphoweave.gif that I could not find in the file listing, and long pipelines run on the GUI thread with processEvents pumping and no re-entrancy guard. Review of Landmark Transfer and Surface Segmentation is partial (large files).

safety.rationale: Searched all files for network, subprocess, eval/exec, pickle and torch: no data transmission, no download-and-execute, np.load uses allow_pickle=False (MorphoWeaveModelLibrary.py:237). The one concrete weakness is unvalidated database names in Model Library ingest (MorphoWeaveModelLibrary.py:573-575) allowing writes outside the library root, and shutil.rmtree on a user-selected folder (line 199) guarded only by a confirmation dialog.

environment.rationale: No installs at import; dependencies are installed only from the Landmark Transfer widget via slicer.packaging.pip_ensure with a confirmation prompt (MorphoWeaveLandmarkTransfer.py:203-218), and no torch/PyTorch index is used. However pip_uninstall(["tiny3d", "tiny3d-rs"]) removes packages from Slicer's shared environment, which can break other extensions that import tiny3d; no sys.path or global logging changes were found.

packaging.rationale: Each module CMakeLists installs its script plus Resources/Python/__init__.py and PoseEMTemplate.py (MorphoWeaveLandmarkTransfer/CMakeLists.txt:9-13), and registered test files exist; EXTENSION_DEPENDS "" matches build_dependencies []. But README.md:2 and CMakeLists.txt:10 reference logo.png and README.md:22 references Docs/Media/morphoweave.gif, neither of which appears in the repository file listing at this revision, so the catalog icon URL may 404.

license.rationale: LICENSE is BSD 2-Clause (Arthur Porto, 2025) permitting redistribution, and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md reproduces the BSD 2-Clause notice for the SlicerDenseCorrespondenceAnalysis/DeCAL code that Atlas Builder was adapted from. The runtime pip dependencies tiny3d-rs and rustcpd are not bundled, so their licenses were not verified here.

soundness.rationale: Modules follow the ScriptedLoadableModule structure, heavy imports are inside functions, render pausing is restored in finally blocks, and errors are surfaced with errorDisplay/status text. Weaknesses: long pipelines run on the GUI thread with qt.QApplication.processEvents() pumping (MorphoWeaveAtlasBuilder.py:1005-1008, MorphoWeaveModelLibrary.py:589) with no cancel and no re-entrancy guard on the Run button, and Model Library reads JSON with an unclosed handle (MorphoWeaveModelLibrary.py:106).

utility.rationale: README.md documents all four modules, outputs, dependencies and troubleshooting, tutorial/README.md is an illustrated walkthrough with an external sample dataset, and each module ships unittest-based tests registered as ctest. Overlap with SlicerMorph/DeCAL is explicitly discussed and attributed.

findings.title: Model Library ingest does not validate the database name (path traversal / writes outside library root)
findings.evidence:
dbName = self.ssmNameEditor.text or Path(self.ssmTemplateModelSelector.currentPath).stem
    dbRootPath = self.databasePathSelector.currentPath
    db_path = os.path.join(dbRootPath, dbName)

    if os.path.exists(db_path):
findings.explanation: The name typed in 'New Database Name' is joined to the library root without any check, so a name such as '../atlas' or 'a/b' makes ingestSSMDatabase create directories and copy files outside the configured library folder. The same unvalidated path is later passed to removeSSMDatabase, which calls shutil.rmtree(dbPath) (line 199) after a single confirmation dialog, so a mis-typed or crafted name can delete a directory the user did not intend. Atlas Builder already implements the correct guard (isSafeLibraryName, MorphoWeaveAtlasBuilder.py:536-545) but Model Library does not reuse it.
findings.suggestion: Reuse MorphoWeaveAtlasBuilderLogic.isSafeLibraryName (or an equivalent check) in onIngestButton and in Atlas Builder's _saveSsmToLibrary path, and refuse names containing separators, '..' or reserved characters before creating or deleting anything.

findings.title: pip_uninstall of tiny3d/tiny3d-rs modifies Slicer's shared Python environment
findings.evidence:
if legacy_tiny3d_installed:
        slicer.packaging.pip_uninstall(["tiny3d", "tiny3d-rs"])

      slicer.packaging.pip_ensure(
        requirements,
        prompt_install=not legacy_tiny3d_installed,
        requester="Landmark Transfer",
      )
findings.explanation: Installing tiny3d-rs/rustcpd is user-confirmed and acceptable, but the code also uninstalls the legacy 'tiny3d' distribution from Slicer's shared environment. Any other installed extension that imports tiny3d (for example a SlicerMorph-style point-cloud workflow) stops working after this action, for a user who only wanted to run MorphoWeave. The confirmation dialog at lines 203-206 mentions the removal, which limits the surprise, but the impact on other extensions is not stated.
findings.suggestion: State in the confirmation dialog that other extensions using tiny3d will stop working, and prefer installing tiny3d-rs without removing tiny3d when the two can coexist, or document the conflict in the module help text.

findings.title: README and EXTENSION_ICONURL reference logo.png and Docs/Media/morphoweave.gif that are not in the file listing
findings.explanation: The repository listing at this revision contains Docs/Images/nsf-logo.png and tutorial/images/*.png but no root logo.png and no Docs/Media directory, while README.md:2 uses and README.md:22 uses Docs/Media/morphoweave.gif. If those files are genuinely absent, the catalog icon URL 404s and the README renders broken images. The automated scan reported these two files as present but unreadable, so this may be a tooling limitation rather than a defect; it should be confirmed against the commit.
findings.suggestion: Confirm logo.png and Docs/Media/morphoweave.gif exist at the reviewed commit (or add them / point EXTENSION_ICONURL at an existing file such as Docs/Images/nsf-logo.png).

findings.title: Long pipelines run on the GUI thread with processEvents pumping and no re-entrancy guard
findings.evidence:
now = time.monotonic()
        if done == total or (now - last_ui_pump >= 0.10):
          qt.QApplication.processEvents()
          last_ui_pump = now
findings.explanation: Atlas Builder alignment/export and Model Library ingest (MorphoWeaveModelLibrary.py:589) run synchronously on the GUI thread and call processEvents to keep the UI alive. Because the Run button is not disabled during the run (self.runBtn is only enabled/disabled by _reeval, line 308), a second click during a pumped event loop can start a second pipeline that writes into the same output/library folders, and there is no cancel path for long runs. This is a usability/robustness issue, not a data-safety one, since outputs go to timestamped folders.
findings.suggestion: Disable the Run/Ingest buttons for the duration of the pipeline (or move the work to a slicer.util.ProgressDialog / CLI-style worker) and add a cancellation check between specimens.

findings.title: Unclosed file handles and first-markup assumption when reading markup files
findings.explanation: json.load(open(...)) leaves the file handle to garbage collection, and only the first entry of the 'markups' array is read, so a .mrk.json containing several markup nodes silently yields the wrong point set. Neither is a safety issue; both are ordinary robustness nits.
findings.suggestion: Use a with-block and either validate that exactly one markup node is present or merge all fiducial nodes.

findings.title: Submission doc tells the author what to state in the index PR; no reviewer-directed instructions found
findings.evidence:
State that:

- The repository follows the recommended `Slicer+ExtensionName` naming convention while the extension remains displayed as MorphoWeave in Slicer.
- The extension operates locally and does not upload user data.
findings.explanation: This is author-facing publication guidance, not an attempt to instruct AI reviewers to skip checks, so it is not a manipulation finding. I independently confirmed the claim: the only URLs in the code are documentation/help links, and no network, telemetry or upload code exists in the files I read.

findings.title: Several megabytes of images committed to the repository
findings.explanation: The tutorial images total roughly 5 MB and the animated GIF is reported at about 4 MB. This is acceptable for documentation but is on the heavy side for a source repository; it does not affect the built extension.
findings.suggestion: Consider hosting the animation externally or compressing it.
